config.title: Grader Submit
config.displayLanguage.description: Language of the Grader panel, statement viewer, messages and status bar. Changes apply at once. Command names and settings follow VS Code's own display language. Grader content (problem names, compiler messages) is never translated.
config.displayLanguage.enum.auto: The language VS Code is displayed in (Thai if VS Code is in Thai, otherwise English)
config.panel.sections.description: Sections of the Grader panel, in the order shown. Remove one to hide it; reorder the list to move them. **Account** always comes back while you are logged out (it holds the login form). Empty = all sections.
config.panel.sections.current: Current problem: the open file's problem, counted score, language and Submit
config.panel.sections.result: Result: the latest submission's verdict per test
config.panel.sections.history: History: every submission for the problem
config.panel.sections.trophies: Trophies: first full scores, your streak and progress per topic (shown while the fun extras are on)
config.panel.sections.problems: Problems: all problems with their counted score
config.panel.look.description: How the panel, the Test view and the statement look.
config.panel.look.subtle: Short animations, section headers that stay in view, raised cards, and frosted menus and tooltips when VS Code's own are frosted.
config.panel.look.plain: No animations, pinned headers or frost.
config.panel.compact.description: Compact panel: tighter spacing, the counted score on one line, one-line problem rows (full name in the tooltip) and smaller verdict tiles.
config.panel.topicClickOrder.description: What a click on a topic pill in the Problems list does first. Each click moves to the next state; the third click turns the topic filter off again.
config.panel.topicClickOrder.showFirst: First click shows only problems with that topic, the second hides them, the third turns it off.
config.panel.topicClickOrder.hideFirst: First click hides problems with that topic, the second shows only them, the third turns it off.
config.baseUrl.description: Base URL of the cafe-grader-web server. Read from user settings only (a workspace cannot change where your password is sent).
config.username.description: Your grader login name. The password is stored in the OS keychain (VS Code SecretStorage), never in settings.
config.pollIntervalSeconds.description: Seconds between status checks while a submission is graded (minimum 3). Polling only runs right after a submission and stops after 3 minutes.
config.confirmBeforeSubmit.description: Ask once before submitting a file whose problem was matched automatically (by file name or folder name). Submitting saves the match as your choice, so it isn't asked again. Problems you chose yourself are never asked; suggestions always are.
config.saveBeforeSubmit.description: Save the file before submitting, so the grader gets exactly what is on disk. Save actions such as format on save run first. Turn off to submit the editor's text without saving.
config.revealResultAfterSubmit.descripti: When grading finishes, open the **Result** section in the panel and scroll it into view. Keyboard focus stays in your editor.
config.debugRequests.description: Log every grader request (method, path, status) and cache hit/miss to the **Grader Submit: Requests** output channel, to check request counts. Never logs passwords or tokens.
config.statementBeside.description: Open problem statements in an editor tab beside your code.
config.panelOpenOnStartup.description: Open the panel when a window starts. Your cursor stays where it is.
config.statementFollowsFile.description: An open statement tab switches to the problem of the file you switch to, and closes when that source file has no problem.
config.defaultLanguage.description: Language for "New file for this problem" when the active file's language isn't allowed and no language was used before (e.g. C++, Python, Java). Archive and other non-source languages are never chosen automatically.
config.fileNamePattern.description: File name for **New file for this problem** and **Rename file to match the problem**. `{name}` = the problem name, `{id}` = the problem id, `{ext}` = the language's extension; must end with `.{ext}`. Files named this way are also matched to their problem automatically. Example: `{id}_{name}.{ext}` → `1360_00_Intro_11.cpp`.
config.runner.defaultTimeLimitSeconds.de: Time limit (seconds) for a test run when the grader doesn't give one.
config.runner.defaultMemoryLimitMB.descr: Memory limit (MB) for a test run when the grader doesn't give one. The figure is an estimate, and Windows doesn't measure it.
config.runner.compilerPaths.description: Paths of the tools that run your code, by tool name, for example `{ "g++": "/opt/gcc/bin/g++" }`. Without an entry the tool is found on `PATH`.
config.runner.extraCompileArgs.descripti: Extra compiler arguments by language (`cpp`, `c`, `java`, `rust`, `go`, `haskell`), for example `{ "cpp": ["-fsanitize=address"] }`.
config.cacheMaxMB.description: Size limit (MB) for downloaded problem statements and test cases. When it is exceeded, the least recently used files are deleted first. Files unused for 30 days are removed automatically. Use **Grader: Clear Cached Data…** to clear everything.
color.explorer.solved.description: Explorer badge and file name: full score.
color.explorer.inProgress.description: Explorer badge and file name: submitted, score below full.
color.explorer.zero.description: Explorer badge and file name: submitted, score 0.
color.explorer.untried.description: Explorer badge and file name: not tried yet.
color.explorer.tag.description: Explorer badge and file name: one of the colours given to tags.
config.explorer.badge.description: What the badge beside a file in the Explorer shows. Only files with a problem get one.
config.explorer.badge.score: The counted score: ✓ for full score, – if not tried yet.
config.explorer.badge.tag: Two letters of the problem's first topic tag.
config.explorer.colors.description: Colour Explorer badges and file names by score or tag. Turn off to keep the normal text colour.

config.fun.enabled.description: Turn on the fun extras: the celebration for a first full score, trophies, and the break reminder. Off turns all of them off; Play Celebration and Take a Break still work.
config.fun.celebrate.description: Celebrate the first time a problem passes every test or reaches a counted score of 100.
config.fun.breakReminder.description: After a long stretch of work, suggest a short break: first a hint in the status bar, then, only at a natural stopping point, a small prompt (at most twice a day).
config.fun.breakMinutes.description: Minutes of work (edits, runs and submits; a gap of 10 minutes starts the count again) before the break hint appears.
config.fun.breakScene.sand: Your code falls like sand; push it, scoop it, pour it.
config.fun.breakScene.donut3d: Your code spins into a 3D donut.
config.fun.breakScene.donut2d: Your code spins into a text donut.
config.fun.breakScene.breathe: Your code forms a ring that grows and shrinks with your breath.
config.fun.breakScene.swarm: Your code swirls after the mouse.
